config.footerNote: Original practice questions written to the published AQA GCSE Religious Studies A (8062) specification, Component 1: Catholic Christianity, using the question format examined from June 2026 (1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks). Not past-paper material. Model answers are indicative exemplars, not official AQA mark schemes; other valid answers are credited in the exam.

Beliefs.1: AO1. Two 1-mark items open each question. (a) Multiple choice: four options, one correct answer – give the letter and the answer. (b) Short answer ('Give one…' / 'Name one…'): only the first answer given is credited, so write one precise point.
Beliefs.4: AO1. 'Explain two ways in which… influences Catholics today' (AO1.2) or 'Explain two different Christian beliefs/views about…' (AO1.3). For each of the two points: 1 mark for a simple, relevant and accurate explanation; 2 marks for a detailed explanation (developed with an example, evidence, reference to different views or detailed information). For influence questions the development must show clear influence on how Catholics live or act; for 'different' questions the two points must genuinely differ.
Beliefs.6: AO1.1. 'Explain two Catholic beliefs/teachings about… Refer to sacred writings or another source of Christian belief and teaching in your answer.' For each of two beliefs: 1 mark simple explanation, 2 marks detailed explanation (4 max). Source of authority: 2 marks for naming AND applying a relevant source (e.g. a Bible passage, the Catechism, a Church document, the Creed) to the question; 1 mark for naming one without applying it, or for applying one without naming it.
Beliefs.12: AO2. Evaluate a statement: arguments in support, arguments against (including different Christian or non-religious views where relevant) and a justified conclusion. Levels: L4 (10–12) well-argued, reasoned consideration of different points of view, logical chains of reasoning leading to judgement(s) supported by knowledge of relevant evidence, references to religion applied to the issue; L3 (7–9) reasoned consideration of different points of view with logical chains of reasoning and clear reference to religion; L2 (4–6) reasoned consideration of one point of view, or recognition of different views each supported by reasons (max L2 if no reference to religion); L1 (1–3) a point of view with reasons stated; 0 nothing worthy of credit. Up to 3 further marks for spelling, punctuation, grammar and specialist terms.

Practices.1: AO1. Two 1-mark items open each question. (a) Multiple choice: four options, one correct answer – give the letter and the answer. (b) Short answer ('Give one…' / 'Name one…'): only the first answer given is credited, so write one precise point.
Practices.4: AO1. 'Explain two ways in which… influences Catholics today' (AO1.2) or 'Explain two different Christian beliefs/views about…' (AO1.3). For each of the two points: 1 mark for a simple, relevant and accurate explanation; 2 marks for a detailed explanation (developed with an example, evidence, reference to different views or detailed information). For influence questions the development must show clear influence on how Catholics live or act; for 'different' questions the two points must genuinely differ.
Practices.6: AO1.1. 'Explain two ways/reasons/teachings… Refer to sacred writings or another source of Christian belief and teaching in your answer.' For each of two points: 1 mark simple explanation, 2 marks detailed explanation (4 max). Source of authority: 2 marks for naming AND applying a relevant source (e.g. a Bible passage, the Catechism, a Church document) to the question; 1 mark for naming one without applying it, or for applying one without naming it.
Practices.12: AO2. Evaluate a statement: arguments in support, arguments against (including different Christian or non-religious views where relevant) and a justified conclusion. Levels: L4 (10–12) well-argued, reasoned consideration of different points of view, logical chains of reasoning leading to judgement(s) supported by knowledge of relevant evidence, references to religion applied to the issue; L3 (7–9) reasoned consideration of different points of view with logical chains of reasoning and clear reference to religion; L2 (4–6) reasoned consideration of one point of view, or recognition of different views each supported by reasons (max L2 if no reference to religion); L1 (1–3) a point of view with reasons stated; 0 nothing worthy of credit. Up to 3 further marks for spelling, punctuation, grammar and specialist terms.
